channel.description: UN News - Global perspective Human stories | Asia Pacific

item.title: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
item.description: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Malaysia: UN agency urges safeguards after refugees returned to Myanmar
item.description: The UN refugee agency, UNHCR, has voiced concern over Malaysia’s decision to return 1,476 people to Myanmar amid an ongoing civil war and a dire human rights and humanitarian situation.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: DPR Korea tells UN its nuclear status is ‘irreversible’, rejects outside pressure
item.description: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) told the UN General Assembly on Monday that its status as a nuclear-armed State was irreversible, arguing that its military capabilities were necessary to safeguard the country’s sovereignty and maintain peace on the Korean Peninsula.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Countries far from conflict paying the price for wars not their own, India tells UN
item.description: India’s External Affairs Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar warned on Saturday that violent conflicts continue to undermine international peace and security, while countries far removed from the battlefield are being forced to pay a heavy price.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Tuvalu urges decisive global action as rising seas threaten its future
item.description: Climate change remains the greatest existential threat to Tuvalu, Prime Minister Feleti Teo told the UN General Assembly on Friday, warning that the pace and scale of international action are still falling far short of what vulnerable island nations need.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nepal PM urges climate justice after ‘Himalayan tsunami’ devastates country
item.description: Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah brought a stark warning from the Himalayas to the UN General Assembly on Thursday, saying catastrophic floods that killed at least 1,400 people in his country laid bare the human cost of climate change, and the failure of the international system to protect those least responsible for it.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Australia urges global cooperation on climate, AI checks and international law
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese underlined the need for countries to work together to address the climate crisis, emerging technologies such as AI, and the breakdown of international rules, at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Rohingya refugees deserve a future beyond survival, not endless displacement
item.description: Nine years after the mass displacement of the Rohingya from Myanmar, their situation remains one of the world's most protracted and complex refugee crises, marked by years of persecution and uncertainty over the prospect of returning home.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: When a country goes underwater: Island States fight for their future
item.description: Rising sea levels and ever-more-powerful storms are eroding shorelines, submerging land and threatening to evict millions of people from their homes worldwide.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nepal floods: ‘Apocalyptic’ destruction signals wider climate threat across Himalayas
item.description: The catastrophic flooding that swept away entire villages in northern Nepal could occur again in the country or elsewhere in the Himalayas due to climate change.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN fact-finding mission on Iran focuses on plight of civilians
item.description: The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran confirmed that civilians in the country suffered serious human rights violations and “crimes against humanity committed by their government,” while finding "reasonable grounds" to believe that the United States committed “war crimes” in the context of its ongoing conflict with the Islamic Republic.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: ‘Being a woman is a crime in Afghanistan,’ civil society briefer declares
item.description: Since the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021, the continuing presence of terrorist groups as well as rights violations against women and girls are a growing concern as the Security Council met Wednesday to hear latest developments, including from a civil society representative who said being born as a woman in the country “is a crime”. Follow full coverage here.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UNICEF says thousands of children require mental health support after Nepal floods
item.description: Three weeks after the devastating flash floods in Nepal, about 17,000 children require urgent mental health and psychosocial support in the country, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Flood-ravaged Nepal calls for climate justice
item.description: Nepal’s call for financial compensation following recent deadly floods underlines the need to help countries that contribute the least to climate change – but are increasingly grappling with its most lethal consequences, the top UN official in the country said on Wednesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Plight of Afghans going ‘from bad to worse’, but the world is looking away: Türk
item.description: Since the Taliban returned to power in 2021, the plight of Afghans has only deteriorated, with millions impoverished while authorities violate basic human rights daily.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN aims to raise nearly $50 million for Nepal flood response
item.description: The UN and its humanitarian partners launched a $49.6 million flash appeal on Friday to deliver emergency assistance to more than 84,000 people affected by last week’s catastrophic floods in Nepal.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nepal floods leave 22,000 children without safe water: UNICEF
item.description: More than a week after flash floods struck the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli river basin in Nepal, at least 22,000 children urgently need safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene support, the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nepal floods: Mounting death toll and concern for women and girls
item.description: As rescue efforts continue in Nepal, humanitarians are focused on how the recent deadly flash floods have impacted women and girls, as well as access to healthcare.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Nepal flooding deaths surpass 900 as needs climb
item.description: The confirmed death toll from Nepal’s catastrophic floods has surged to 903, with more than 4,200 still missing as rescue crews and humanitarian workers battle blocked highways to reach the hardest-hit areas, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: As the Himalayas melt, deadly floods become the new normal
item.description: A day before a wall of ice, rock and muddy water tore through Himalayan valleys along the Nepal-China border, Dipesh Chapagain was discussing with a colleague just how devastating such a disaster could be.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Immense impact’ of Nepal flood disaster highlighted as casualties mount
item.description: The impact of the deadly flood in Nepal has been described as “immense” as the authorities there confirm that 538 bodies have been recovered from the disaster-stricken area.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Deadly floods cause widespread destruction in China, Nepal
item.description: Severe flooding in the Tibet autonomous region of China and Nepal caused widespread destruction and mounting death tolls, UN agencies reported on Wednesday as aid efforts deployed to help provide emergency assistance.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: One million children in Afghanistan face deadly malnutrition
item.description: Some 3.7 million children in Afghanistan are suffering from wasting, one of the most dangerous forms of malnutrition, with around one million currently battling the most severe, life-threatening form of the condition.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Rohingyas in Myanmar suffering ‘heartbreaking’ misery and cruelty
item.description: Members of the minority ethnic Rohingya Muslim group in Myanmar are “suffering, misery, and cruelty on multiple levels and across the country that is heartbreaking,” according to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Singapore: Independent rights experts urge immediate end to ‘unlawful use’ of death penalty
item.description: Independent UN Human Rights Council-appointed experts on Tuesday condemned the execution of at least 16 people in Singapore for drug-related offences this year and urged the country to end its “continued and unlawful use of capital punishment.”
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Five years after Taliban takeover, Afghan women ‘erased from public life’
item.description: Five years after the Taliban seized power, women and girls in Afghanistan have been systematically stripped of their rights, UN agencies said on Wednesday. De facto authorities have issued more than 100 decrees curbing education, work and freedom of movement – restrictions now compounded by deep cuts to aid on the ground.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Myanmar: UN investigators document deliberate military attacks on civilians
item.description: Myanmar's military has carried out a sustained campaign of deliberate attacks on civilians – including airstrikes on homes, schools and camps for displaced people, alongside arbitrary detention, torture and sexual violence – according to Human Rights Council-appointed investigators.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Afghanistan: UN tells Taliban to open up on abuses committed by security forces
item.description: Five years into Taliban rule, Afghans still have almost no way of knowing whether soldiers, police and morality officers who abuse their power ever face consequences – and that secrecy is corroding trust in the State, the UN said Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Returning Afghans face growing risk of trafficking as crises deepen
item.description: Afghans returning from neighbouring countries are facing growing risks of human trafficking and exploitation as overlapping humanitarian and economic crises leave many struggling to survive, the UN warned on Thursday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: A hijab inspection, a slap, a warning letter: Inside three months of Taliban rule
item.description: A woman is stopped for buying groceries alone. The shopkeeper who served her is slapped and hauled in for questioning. A teacher is turned away from her own classroom for wearing the wrong cloak.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
